第 35 章 Get Deployment Right on Day One第一天就把部署做对

James Turnbull / 詹姆斯·特恩布尔

— 第 105 页 —

Deployment gets the code you and your team have written out into the world. Any system you've written that isn't deployed and in front of a user isn't generating value. It's also not giving you feedback about your product and how it helps your users. Hence, getting deployment going is one of the first things most engineering teams (even if that's just you on day one!) do when they begin to build a product.

部署把你和团队写的代码送到世界上。任何你写了但没部署、没在用户面前的系统都不产生价值。它也不会给你关于产品和它如何帮助用户的反馈。因此，让部署跑起来是大多数工程团队（即使第一天只有你一个人！）开始构建产品时最先做的事之一。

Like most items constructed at the start of a company or product's life, we often create the fastest, simplest solution hack as our deployment system: "I just need something that works, and I'll worry about making it better later." This is a mistake.

就像公司或产品生命初期构建的大多数东西一样，我们经常用最快最简单的 hack 作为部署系统：「我只需要能跑的东西，以后再改进。」这是个错误。

The system that gets your code from your engineers to the customer is the most crucial piece of engineering tooling you'll build—ever.

把你的代码从工程师送到客户手里的系统，是你将构建的最关键的工程工具——有史以来。

The capabilities, quality, and performance of your deployment system directly correlate to the speed to market of your product, both in generating value and addressing user feedback and issues. Not only this, your deployment frequency and outcomes represent one of the (rare) early measurements of engineering velocity and quality. If your product or business partners are complaining about things moving too slow, this is one of the first places you should look. Finally, getting code in front of users and seeing your product in action makes your engineers happy.

你的部署系统的能力、质量和性能直接关系到产品上市速度，包括产生价值和处理用户反馈与问题。不仅如此，你的部署频率和结果代表了工程速度和质量的（稀有）早期衡量指标之一。如果你的产品或业务伙伴抱怨事情进展太慢，这是你应该首先看的地方之一。最后，把代码放到用户面前、看到产品在运行让工程师快乐。

You might get a lot of pressure to develop features and not spend time on this kind of tooling, as a manager you need to make sure that you have given the team room to develop this tooling.

你可能面临很多压力要开发功能而不是花时间在这种工具上，作为经理你需要确保给团队空间来开发这种工具。

— 第 106 页 —

Building That Deployment System构建那个部署系统

When you build that crucial first deployment system, you need to build upon the appropriate principles: what can be summarized as "CI/CD," or Continuous Integration/Continuous Delivery:

当你构建那个关键的第一个部署系统时，你需要基于正确的原则：可以总结为「CI/CD」，即持续集成/持续交付：

  • Everybody should be able to deploy.每个人都应该能部署。
  • Deployment should be automatic and continuous.部署应该是自动且持续的。

You can then scale your deployment system instead of refactoring it every time your organization scales. This comes with some risk of premature optimization but I believe that risk is outweighed by the rewards: faster deployment, enhanced developer happiness, and faster speed to market. Let's look at each principle.

然后你可以扩展你的部署系统而不是每次组织扩展时重构它。这带有一些过早优化的风险，但我相信回报超过了风险：更快的部署、更强的开发者幸福感、更快的上市速度。让我们看看每个原则。

Everyone Should Be Able to Deploy每个人都应该能部署

Everyone on your team should be able to deploy (Figure 35-1). A good deployment system should be continuous and not gated. Deployment systems triggered by intermediaries, "approvers," or small groups, like QA teams, are inherently hamstrung. First, this model removes a developer's ownership of the deployment of their code and its outcomes. Worse, it sometimes transfers ownership of the code that is being deployed, disconnecting an engineer from the reality of the systems for which they write code. Second, these models are slow by design. They exist to put roadblocks in the way of your code being deployed.

你团队里每个人都应该能部署（图 35-1）。一个好的部署系统应该是持续的、不设门槛的。由中间人、「审批者」或像 QA 团队这样的小群体触发的部署系统天生就有缺陷。首先，这个模式剥夺了开发者对自己代码部署及其结果的所有权。更糟的是，它有时转移了被部署代码的所有权，让工程师和他们写代码的系统的现实脱节。其次，这些模式天生就慢。它们存在的目的就是在你的代码部署路上放路障。

— 第 107 页 —

Figure 35-1. Every team member must have the ability to deploy

图 35-1：每个团队成员都必须有部署能力（图示）

Deployment Should Be Automatic and Continuous部署应该是自动且持续的

Code sitting in repositories or in branches is also not adding value. Any deployment process should optimize for putting the system into use as fast as possible. My preference has always been to automatically deploy to production any code merged to "master," as demonstrated in Figure 35-2.

放在仓库或分支里的代码也不产生价值。任何部署流程都应该优化为尽快让系统投入使用。我一直的偏好是自动部署任何合并到「master」的代码到生产环境，如图 35-2 所示。

Figure 35-2. Automatically deploying from "master" to production

图 35-2：从「master」自动部署到生产环境（图示）

— 第 108 页 —

There has also always been a lot of debate over how to manage development and code branching processes to get that code merged. Again, my personal preference has always been to make use of GitHub flow, which states:

关于如何管理开发和代码分支流程来合并代码也一直有很多争论。同样，我个人的偏好一直是使用 GitHub flow，它规定：

  1. The "master" branch can always be deployed.「master」分支随时可以部署。
  2. Everything is branched off "master" and named for a feature or issue.一切从「master」切分支，以功能或 issue 命名。
  3. Do your work on that branch locally and regularly push your work upstream to the server.在那个分支上本地工作，定期把工作推到服务器。
  4. Merge by opening a pull request, having it reviewed, and then merging it to "master."通过开 Pull Request、评审、然后合并到「master」来合并。
  5. Automatically deploy "master."自动部署「master」。

Figure 35-3. Deploying using a "master" branch

图 35-3：用「master」分支部署（图示）

With the GitHub flow, we optimize for small, short-lived branches to reduce the risk of merge conflicts and disruption and to increase the velocity of code being pushed and deployed. Your commit-to-deploy time is another good, early measure of your team's development velocity.

用 GitHub flow，我们优化小而短命的分支来减少合并冲突和中断的风险，提高代码推送和部署的速度。你的提交到部署时间是另一个好的早期团队开发速度衡量指标。

If you are worried about interdependencies or features being developed over longer time frames—for example, in stages—you can make use of feature flags to hide features that aren't ready for prime time or not yet complete. Feature flags also encourage early user and integration testing. They additionally provide your engineers with a sense that a feature is evolving and work is progressing rather than being stuck in a long-lived branch.

如果你担心相互依赖或跨更长时间框架开发的功能——例如分阶段——你可以用 feature flag 来隐藏还没准备好上线或还没完成的功能。Feature flag 还鼓励早期用户和集成测试。它们还让工程师感觉功能在演进、工作在推进，而不是卡在一个长命分支里。

— 第 109 页 —

If you do have to put in an approval process to satisfy compliance or regulatory requirements, the GitHub flow allows you to lock off the "master" branch from direct pushes and require approvals on pull requests.

如果你确实需要加审批流程来满足合规或监管要求，GitHub flow 允许你锁定「master」分支禁止直接 push，要求 PR 审批。

Deployment FTW部署万岁

After you have a deployment system that provides everyone on your team the ability to deploy automatically and continuously, the return on investment will be tangible and measurable. If your deployment system meets these two objectives, you're building on a good foundation that will allow you to scale as your team and company grow.

当你有了一个让团队每个人都能自动持续部署的系统后，投资回报将是有形且可衡量的。如果你的部署系统满足这两个目标，你就在一个好的基础上构建，这个基础将让你随着团队和公司成长而扩展。
